explanations.answer: The seed of man and of beast
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “…I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and of beast.” Think about that for a second. He's sowing PEOPLE and animals like they're a crop. The only thing I've ever sowed is flour all over my counter.

explanations.answer: The seed of wheat and of barley
explanations.explanation: Good guess, since a farmer sowing a field does make you think of grain. But the verse says the LORD will sow them with “…the seed of man and of beast.” Wheat is a baker's best friend, so I wanted it to be wheat too. The text just doesn't say it.

explanations.answer: The seed of vine and of olive
explanations.explanation: Vines and olives sound like a fine field, friend. But that's not what the LORD says here. He says He will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah “…with the seed of man and of beast.” The picture is about people and animals filling the land again.

Plant it is, baker. The LORD says, “…so I will watch over them to build and to plant…” and He says it with the same watching He used for the uprooting. Uprooting and tearing down on one side, building and planting on the other. I know a little about being put away in the dark and then set somewhere new, and I can tell you the second part is better.

I see why that one tempts you, since the first half of the verse is heavy. But the LORD doesn't say scatter here. He says, “…so I will watch over them to build and to plant…” The second half turns toward something good. It's the same watching, now aimed at building.

That's a reasonable thought, friend, but the word isn't in this verse. The LORD says He will watch over them “…to build and to plant…” The words before it, uproot, tear down, demolish, destroy, are the hard part. This is the part where it turns around.

True. The LORD says, “Instead, each will die for his own iniquity.” Then He adds, “If anyone eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.” So whoever eats the sour grapes is the one who makes the face. I've eaten a lemon cookie once by accident and I'm still not over it.

It's actually true, baker, and here's what the text says. The LORD says, “Instead, each will die for his own iniquity.” The old saying about the fathers eating the sour grapes goes away. In its place, “If anyone eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.”

Egypt, yes! The LORD says the new covenant will not be like the one He made with their fathers “…when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt…” Taken by the hand. That's a picture I like a lot, friend. I know what it's like when somebody finally reaches in and takes hold of you.

Babylon's a name people know, so I get the pull. But the verse names a different land. The LORD says He took their fathers by the hand “…to lead them out of the land of Egypt…” That's the covenant the new one is being compared to.

Assyria is a big name, so I see why it came to mind, baker. But this verse points somewhere else. The LORD says the earlier covenant was made when He took their fathers by the hand to lead them “…out of the land of Egypt…” That's the land to remember here.

explanations.answer: In their minds and on their hearts
explanations.explanation: Right on, baker. The LORD says, “I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.” Not just somewhere they have to go look at it. It goes inside them.

I understand the thought, friend. But the verse doesn't mention tablets at all. The LORD says, “I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.” This time the law goes inside the people.

explanations.answer: On the doorposts of their houses
explanations.explanation: A doorpost is a place you'd see every day, so that's a smart guess. But the LORD names two other places. He says, “I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.” The new covenant is written on the people themselves.

That's the reason, baker. The LORD says no one will need to say, “Know the LORD…” “because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest…” That's everybody, the least to the greatest. Nobody gets left standing at the back of the line.

explanations.answer: They will each own a scroll
explanations.explanation: A scroll for everyone would be handy, friend. But the verse gives a different reason. The LORD says no longer will each man teach his neighbor or his brother to know Him, because “…they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest…” No scroll is mentioned.

explanations.answer: They will all see His signs
explanations.explanation: Signs are a big deal in the Bible, so I see where that came from. But this verse doesn't say signs. The LORD says no longer will each man teach his neighbor or his brother to know Him, because “…they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest…” The reason is simply that they will know Him.

Close, but the statement is false, baker, and here's what the LORD says. “For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.” He forgives, and He remembers their sins no more. That's Jeremiah 31:34, and it leaves no room for "still remembers."

False, and that's the good news. The LORD says, “For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.” Forgiven, and remembered no more. Friend, that's the kind of promise you read twice just to make sure it's still there.

explanations.answer: Only if that order left His presence
explanations.explanation: That's it. The LORD says, “Only if this fixed order departed from My presence, declares the LORD, would Israel’s descendants ever cease to be a nation before Me.” The fixed order is the sun by day and the moon and stars by night. Those just keep showing up. I hope that's the kind of promise it is, baker.

explanations.answer: If they broke His covenant again
explanations.explanation: Earlier, the LORD did say they broke the old covenant (Jeremiah 31:32), so I see the connection you made. But this verse puts it a different way. The LORD says, “Only if this fixed order departed from My presence…” That's the only condition He names for Israel's descendants to cease to be a nation before Him.

The city rebuilding does come up a few verses later, friend. But it isn't the condition here. The LORD says Israel's descendants would cease to be a nation before Him “Only if this fixed order departed from My presence…” The sun, moon, stars and sea are the measuring stick.

Reject is the word, baker. The LORD says, “Only if the heavens above could be measured and the foundations of the earth below searched out would I reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done…” Measuring the heavens, and I couldn't even measure a cup of flour right on my first day.

Gathering is a nice word, and it's good news, but it isn't what this verse says. The LORD says He would “…reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done…” and only if the heavens could be measured and the earth's foundations searched out. Those are the conditions He names.

Bless would fit the mood, friend, but the LORD's word here is a different one. He says, “…would I reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done…” The condition is measuring the heavens above and searching out the foundations of the earth below.

It's the other way around, baker. The LORD says of the valley of the dead bodies and ashes, the fields, all the way to the Horse Gate, that it “…will be holy to the LORD.” Then He says, “It will never again be uprooted or demolished.” Never again.

False, and the last line says it plain. The LORD says the whole valley of the dead bodies and ashes “…will be holy to the LORD.” Then He finishes with, “It will never again be uprooted or demolished.”
